newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Mycal enjoys jump in group, parent profits.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Mycal enjoys jump in group, parent profits.

text.p: Mycal Corp, a leading Japanese supermarket chain operator, on Monday announced a strong surge in group net profits for the year to February 28, 1997, helped by a revamp of some of its outlets.
Mycal's group net profit soared to 15.2 billion yen in 1996/97 from the previous year's 1.01 billion yen. The company predicted profits would rise further to 16 billion yen in 1997/98.
On a parent basis, the company saw a 33.4 percent rise in current profit to 16.03 billion yen in 1996/97 from a year earlier, and predicted a profit of 20 billion yen for 1997/98.
The steep climb in profits was fuelled by healthy sales after a renovation of some Mycal outlets, as well as a good business performance at many of its subsidiaries.

A company spokeswoman told Reuters that 12 out of its 62 subsidiaries whose earnings are fully reflected in the group results turned profitable in 1996/97. Of the total 62 firms, five subsidiaries are newly included in the group earnings.

Mycal subsidiaries includes Mycal Card Co Ltd, a credit card firm, which posted a 74.9 percent jump in current profit to 2.55 billion yen in 1996/97. Meanwhile, Mycal Hokkaido Co Ltd, another Mycal subsidiary, enjoyed a 66.3 percent rise in its current profit to 2.54 billion yen. -- Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-9404
